liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): The opening Shakedown Street gets people moving; Reviewer calls the Shakedown Street nice [28][30]
- **Feel Like a Stranger** (1 review): Brent sounds a little sick on Feel Like a Stranger, per the reviewer [31]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Reviewer singles out He's Gone into Little Star into drums as especially good [27]

## Setlist highlights

- **Maybe You Know**: rare: 6 archived performances [36]
- **Little (Bob) Star**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [36]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-04-15.138067.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 173 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1983-04-15.163649.senn441.neumann.u87.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 182 min [2]
- **gd1983-04-15.fob.miller.94283.sbeok.flac24**: source not stated; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [13]
- **gd1983-04-15.senn421.coyotte.muletaper.88659.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 164 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [16]
- **gd83-04-15s2.sbd.dodd.9975.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 14 songs; 104 min; rated 4.27/5 by 11 [23]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds like an old PCM tape, with no hiss or Dolby artifacts; Crisp, well balanced, vocals out front, and bass present without being overblown [26][27]

## Around the show

- Reviewer, a Kent State student, drove to Buffalo to collect two University at Buffalo friends holding spare guest passes for Rochester [24]
- Reviewer, a Kent State student, drove to Buffalo to collect two University at Buffalo friends holding spare guest passes for Rochester [25]
- The War Memorial was renovated and is now Blue Cross Arena, with better acoustics than in its hockey-barn days [32]
- Reviewer rode up with strangers from Stamford, CT, was stopped by a cop asking about grass, and hallucinated heavily [33]
- Goin' Down the Road into Baby Blue and He's Gone into Little Star came out as filler on Dave's Picks Volume 39 [2]
- Reviewer finds this Bob Star weaker than the Bob Star into Other One at the Meadowlands [26]
- Reviewer calls the first set nothing special and says spring 83 had better moments than this show [30]
- Brent explores more varied keyboard effects in '83 than the jangly sound he seemed stuck on in '81 [31]
- Reviewer thinks Rochester saw better Dead shows in '77 and at Holleder Stadium [32]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-04-15.138067.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 source matrix by Dusborne; Soundboard (shnid:32780), Recording Info: set 1: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k)Set 2: SBD -> PCM -> Dat… [1]
- **gd1983-04-15.163649.senn441.neumann.u87.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) Sennheiser 441's (left + right) + (1) Neumann U87 (center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [2]. Also: Recorded by Rob Eaton, who also did the transfer; Charlie Miller coordinated the effort; Audio Technica and Sennheiser 421 sources from Miller and Ernie Dodd supply a 15:46 patch from Little Star through Drums [2]
- **gd1983-04-15.fob.miller.94283.sbeok.flac24**: taped by Charlie Miller; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Audio Technica Mics -> Cassette Master (Sony D6/Maxell UDXL-II/Dolby B) [13]. Also: Sennheiser 421 front-of-board source, cassette master to DAT to CD, patches Drums and part of Around and Around; Taper sat about 15 feet in front of the soundboard and 10 feet right; it was his first Dead taping; This transfer is Dolby decoded, unlike earlier ones; there is an unpatched cut at the start of Around and Around [13]
- **gd1983-04-15.senn421.coyotte.muletaper.88659.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rick "Coyotte" Colyard; transferred by Muletaper; source: Sennheiser MD421's>Sony D5 (two maxell UD-XL2-S-Cassettes), Location: FOB-11th row DFC @6 ft high on stand (head high) [16]. Also: Sennheiser 421 source with tape flips between Rooster and Dire Wolf, with no loss; Second-set tape starts at the beginning of Little Star, with a flip splice at the start of Around and Around [16]
- **gd83-04-15s2.sbd.dodd.9975.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>PCM>DAT>Sonic Solutions>CDR [23]

claims.text: Reviewer, a Kent State student, drove to Buffalo to collect two University at Buffalo friends holding spare guest passes for Rochester
Reviewer, a Kent State student, drove to Buffalo to collect two University at Buffalo friends holding spare guest passes for Rochester
Soundboard sounds like an old PCM tape, with no hiss or Dolby artifacts
Reviewer finds this Bob Star weaker than the Bob Star into Other One at the Meadowlands
Crisp, well balanced, vocals out front, and bass present without being overblown
Reviewer singles out He's Gone into Little Star into drums as especially good
The opening Shakedown Street gets people moving
Reviewer calls the Shakedown Street nice
Reviewer calls the first set nothing special and says spring 83 had better moments than this show
Brent sounds a little sick on Feel Like a Stranger, per the reviewer
Brent explores more varied keyboard effects in '83 than the jangly sound he seemed stuck on in '81
The War Memorial was renovated and is now Blue Cross Arena, with better acoustics than in its hockey-barn days
Reviewer thinks Rochester saw better Dead shows in '77 and at Holleder Stadium
Reviewer rode up with strangers from Stamford, CT, was stopped by a cop asking about grass, and hallucinated heavily
Recorded by Rob Eaton, who also did the transfer; Charlie Miller coordinated the effort
Audio Technica and Sennheiser 421 sources from Miller and Ernie Dodd supply a 15:46 patch from Little Star through Drums
Goin' Down the Road into Baby Blue and He's Gone into Little Star came out as filler on Dave's Picks Volume 39
Sennheiser 421 front-of-board source, cassette master to DAT to CD, patches Drums and part of Around and Around
Taper sat about 15 feet in front of the soundboard and 10 feet right; it was his first Dead taping
This transfer is Dolby decoded, unlike earlier ones; there is an unpatched cut at the start of Around and Around
Sennheiser 421 source with tape flips between Rooster and Dire Wolf, with no loss
Second-set tape starts at the beginning of Little Star, with a flip splice at the start of Around and Around
